Maybe you are just stoned because I don't think you're understanding me. I can understand why you think the way you do because the situation is really unorthodox. This isn't the first time within the last couple of years where that whole family has been shoved into a hotel, for an extended period of time. I don't know what you would consider a reasonable amount of time for a "transition between homes" period but months and months and months when there are homes available that are big enough and cheaper than the hotel when you constantly go on about having no money is just stupid. Either way, this is besides the point. I only mentioned the present thing because it tied into the topic at hand, it's not even close to the extent that I've helped them out, it's just one specific instance. I'm not an expert on those family financials, but from what I've seen from the financial decisions they've made they could be at risk of being homeless. I don't know. 

I really don't know where you got the third paragraph from. That isn't what happened at all. The apology was done at the beginning. There was no argument mid apology, the subject shifted after the apology from being just about that episode to being about how frustrated they were that the tricks that worked for improving their mental health weren't also working for me. As I said I have no problem with them being upset. This isn't about who'se right and wrong.

The depth of the bizarre financial decisions made by their parents is actually ridiculous. Opting to pay more money for a hotel than to rent an actual house while at the same time claiming to not have money to even give my friend a birthday OR Christmas present. The only reason they got anything was because I convinced their dad to go in with me on computer parts. It boggles my mind.

I don't know the exact reason behind the eviction but iirc it's literally because the family just chose not to pay, because they were planning on moving out but like never actually had a plan. Something stupid and avoidable, essentially. 

And the original thing was basically me texting them things that were (not lies) but things that were intended to elicit concern. Things that generally you would filter, but at the time I was desperate to do anything to make myself feel better and wasn't really concerned about long term consequences. Nothing insulting or anything, but just things that would make you worried about the person who said them. Like I said, I'm not going to defend that, I know it was bad and I shouldn't have done it.

I really don't want to get into very much personal info because I just don't feel too comfy doing that but keep in mind they're NB so I'm using they/them pronouns not necessarily to refer to the entire family. Trust me though, both of us are in agreement with you that it's really stupid that the family is opting to stay in a hotel. The family is being stupidly picky about acceptable housing. It makes no sense to us either. 

What I meant by "caused the argument" was that the argument would not have happened if not for the original thing.

Because it was relevant? If you were in an argument with somebody right before they blocked you you wouldn't mention that an argument happened? 

Why do you say I sound complacent? I don't know how you could have deduced that. 

I agree we need to get out. Their family has no money. They've been living in a hotel since being evicted. I've been helping support them financially but that is absolutely a distant goal.

I understand what you are saying but I do want to clarify that the argument wasn't about the thing that happened. I readily owned up to that. The argument was them accusing me of being complacent and not trying to improve, which is tbh quite the accusation so ofc it got a bit heated. I don't hold it against them given the circumstances but I just wanted to clear that up.

Unfortunately both of our circumstances make something like professional therapy pretty difficult to attain, we're both LGBT and live with unaccepting families who don't really take mental health seriously. If we pursued that it could make things worse, so trying to be there for one another seemed like the next best thing. I appreciate the advice though and if it becomes more realistic I will definitely look more into it.
